name: Texas
about: The blueprint of Texas (perfectnations.com/perfect-states/texas/). Census, NAEP and USDA figures marked "computed" are read by tools/build_us_state.py from data/us/raw/texas/ and data/us-states.json. No figure is estimated.
notes: v1.0: Perfect Texas, a Perfect States blueprint (Preeti Sinha, President and CEO, 25 Nov 2026: "go ahead and implement" the Perfect States plan). Water and Energy are shown as not yet measured: no primary state figure was confirmed.

hero.line: A computed:gdp_words economy where computed:uninsured of Texans had no health insurance in 2025.
hero.sub: Perfect Nations counts what Texas owns, prices the seven basic standards of living for every resident, and designs the capital that closes the gap.

assets.title: Five assets that can carry Perfect Texas.
assets.line: Each is owned by Texans today and can carry a standard of living.

items.name: The Permanent School Fund
items.line: The nation’s oldest and largest educational endowment, set aside by the Texas Constitution for every public school.

items.name: The Rainy Day Fund
items.line: The Economic Stabilization Fund, projected at the end of fiscal 2027, built from oil and gas taxes.

items.name: The land
items.line: State lands and mineral rights stewarded by the General Land Office, earning for the Permanent School Fund.

items.name: The water fund
items.line: Sales tax dedicated by voters to the Texas Water Fund each year from September 2027 to 2047.

items.name: The people
items.line: Texans on 1 July 2025: the asset every other asset serves.

solutions.title: Solutions for Perfect Texas, in order.
solutions.line: Health first: one Texan in six has no insurance, about twice the national rate.

items.challenge: computed:uninsured of Texans had no health insurance in 2025, against computed:uninsured_us nationally.
items.advises: Issue a Texas health-access bond for community clinics in the border and rural counties, repaid from savings in uncompensated hospital care and paid on enrolment and outcomes.

items.challenge: computed:food of households were food insecure in 2022–2024, above the national computed:food_us.
items.advises: Put the savings from SNAP accuracy (band 05) into a food fund with Texas food banks and grocers, county by county, starting in Dimmit County.

items.challenge: computed:reading of fourth graders read at the NAEP Proficient level in 2024.
items.advises: Apply the Permanent School Fund’s guarantee model to reading: an outcome contract, paid only for measured gains, backed by the Fund’s distributions.

solutions.hold: Phase 3, hold the line: shelter (28,031 without a home on one night, January 2025) and livelihood (computed:poverty below the poverty line), with water and energy measured next.

capital.title: Texas already finances at scale.
capital.line: Instruments on record that a Perfect Texas can build on.

items.name: The Bond Guarantee Program
items.line: School district and charter bonds backed by the Permanent School Fund at the end of 2025, lowering what schools pay to borrow.

items.name: School distributions
items.line: Education funding from the Permanent School Fund for the 2026–27 biennium.

items.name: The Texas Water Fund
items.line: Up to $1bn a year of sales tax for water from September 2027 to 2047, approved by voters in November 2025.

intelligence.title: A $725m SNAP bill that accuracy can cut.
intelligence.line: From October 2027 every state pays part of its SNAP food benefits unless at least 94 of every 100 dollars are paid exactly right. AI that checks every case before it is paid can shrink that bill.
intelligence.bill_label: a year in SNAP benefits from October 2027, at the 2025 error rate

facts.label: of SNAP dollars paid in error, 2025
share of benefits the State pays from October 2027

intelligence.advises: Bring the error rate under 8% and the share halves to 5%, about $360m a year saved. Fund AI case review from the savings, starting with the fiscal 2027 rate that sets the bill for fiscal 2030, and audit it every quarter for underpayments as well as overpayments.
